This page contains information about the characters' heights as listed in the [[The Wheel of Time Companion]]. Many of these are referenced in the books themselves and no direct contradictions have been found. Some additional entries have been added that can be inferred from either source and notes and references have been added where this is the case. Non-human characters and creatures will be added at a later date.

= Overview =

Some basic stats from the data left by Robert Jordan:

'''Tallest Man''': [[Nadric]] (7'0" or 2.13m)

'''Tallest Woman''': [[Someryn]] (6'4" or  1.93m)

'''Tallest Non-Aiel Man''': [[Rahvin]] (approx. 6'8" or 2.03m). For purely Third Age characters with listed heights, [[Lan Mandragoran]] is the tallest at 6'5.5" or 1.97m. [[Moridin]] is listed as 6'5" or 6'6" (1.955-1.98m)

'''Tallest Non-Aiel Woman''': [[Varilin Zanaire]] (6'2" or 1.88m)

'''Shortest Man''': [[Raen]] (approx. 5'1" or 1.55m) or [[Wit Congar]] (approx. 5'2" or  1.575m). Both of these depend on the height of their spouses, who are a head taller than them.

'''Shortest Man (confirmed)''': [[Jori]] (5'4" or 1.625m)

'''Shortest Woman''': [[Escaralde Hamdey]], [[Sheraine Caminelle]], [[Ilain Dormaile]] (4'10" or 1.47m)

'''Average height for men in the Westlands''': 5'10" or 1.78m 

'''Average height for women in the Westlands''': 5'5" or 1.65m

'''Average height for Aiel men''': 6'2" or 1.88m

'''Average height for Aiel women''': 5'9" or 1.75m

=Notes on Measurements and Descriptions=
It is worthwhile noting that there is some difference between length [[Measurement|measurements]] in The Wheel of Time and real life. Firstly, there are a different number of inches in a foot. In the [[Westlands]], there are 10" compared to 12" in real life. We know that the heights in the Companion are given in real world measurements, otherwise heights like 5'11" for Mat would not be valid. We also know that feet are the same in both real life and the Westlands by comparing heights that appear in both. Mat doubts Tuon can "stretch to five feet with her heels flat" and Moiraine thinks her father is "an inch short of six feet", which is consistent with their listed heights of 4'11" and 5'11" respectively. A '''hand''' is also a standard measurement with three hands making a foot. This is four inches in real-world terms.

Some other non-standard measures can be inferred from how they are used by Jordan in a consistent way. 

'''Head:''' Can be defined as 8 inches. Examples of this being used to define height differences are Tam/Rand (5'10/6'6"){{ref/book|1|1}}{{ref/book|12|47}}, Elayne/Gawyn (5'7"/6'3"){{ref/book|1|40}} and [[Easar Togita]]/[[Paitar Nachiman]] (5'7"/6'3"){{ref/book|8|p}}. Darlin/Rand (6'0"/6'6"){{ref/book|11|21}} and Perrin/Gaul (6'1"/6'7"){{ref/book|3|34}}{{ref/book|7|3}} are also described as having less than a head's difference between their heights.

'''Head and Shoulders taller''': Can be defined as around 10-12" difference and certainly more than a head as defined above.  Examples where we know both heights are Nisao/Sarin (10"),  Rand/Kiruna (11"), Perrin/Moiraine (11") and Enaila/Somara (12.5").

'''Chest high''': More than head and shoulders. Examples of height differences with this description are Rand/Egwene (15") and Rand/Idrien (13"). It can be used to infer Graendal's height compared to Sammael when disguised as we aren't given her height directly in the Companion.

'''As tall as most men''': Interpreted to be average height for a man. This phrase is used to describe [[Leane Sharif]] (5'10.5"), [[Yurith]] (5'10.5"), [[Shevan Gadarin]] (5'10"), [[Nadere]] (5'11"). [[Masema Dagar]] (5'10") and [[Daved Hanlon]] (5'10"-5'11") are both described as average height. Mat says he's a little taller than most men at 5'11". On the other hand, [[Therava]] (6'0") is described as "taller than most men" , as is [[Dagdara Finchey]] (6'0"), and [[Varilin Zanaire]] (6'2") as "inches taller than most men".

=List of Heights=
The default order in the table below is by height in m. Where a name is marked by a *, it is a best estimate. In cases where the Companion lists two heights for the same person, there are listed in the notes column and they are listed according to the average.

The factions column includes Accepted and novices for Aes Sedai as a means of categorising them all under the same channeler faction. Commoners/nobles shows potential trends between classes. References are given for relevant statements from the books using book abbreviation and chapter in some cases, but not all references are listed.

==Differences from Robert Jordan interviews and correspondences==
Prior to the publication of the Companion, there were a number of statements and answers from Jordan regarding the heights of the main characters. The following table summarises all existing information on this. The heights from the Companion are included for comparison.

Not only do these disagree with the Companion, but they are not consistent even when the interviews are dated close together. According to one of the reporters above: "I definitely got the impression that he cares nothing for the detailed heights and such, but instead goes completely from the mental pictures he's got in his head." This seems a valid statement.

How then does Jordan go from not knowing the heights of the main characters from week to week, to having a list of exact heights for more than 350 characters? The simple answer is that he decided some time after the year 2000 (and publication of Winter's Heart) that he would set these descriptions in stone, possibly in response to being asked it several times by fans. For this reason, the Companion heights are considered canon over these earlier interview responses, especially since they originate ultimately from Robert Jordan's own notes.
